summary: Iteration 4 tested Phase 0 (Access Packs), Phase 1 (Financials -> Activity -> Briefing loop) and Phase 3 (People CRUD + headcount sync) end-to-end. New pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_packs_activity_people.py — 20/20 passed. Full backend suite ran 119 tests: 111 passed, 8 failed. All 8 failures are STALE tests from iterations 1-3 whose assumptions no longer hold under the new pack model or under an OAuth env change (see backend_issues.stale_tests below) — not regressions of the new work. Frontend Playwright: as OWNER, sidebar shows Members + People, People CRUD end-to-end works (add TEST_UI_ person → headcount 6→7 → delete → 6), Members invite with pack='finance' populates a badge, per-member pack dropdown flips FINANCE→HR live, Financials 'Recent activity' strip renders with the latest activities (Removed a revenue entry, Logged revenue, Updated cash → runway…). As MEMBER, sidebar hides Members nav, People page has no add-person-btn, Financials page hides add-entry-btn and edit-settings-btn — read-only enforcement in the UI matches the perm set. Backend + frontend integration: after PUT /financials/settings the summary contains 'cash' + 'runway' and appears as briefing.what_changed[0] with detail '<actor> · <rel time>'. can_write flags on /financials and /people are true for owner and false for member. can_act on /decisions is true for owner and false for member. GET /activities returns newest-first with an 'ago' field. Headcount on /company reflects add/remove of a person. All items from the review-request test matrix passed.

stale_tests.reason: Iteration 3 tests assumed member could write financials. Per iteration 4 spec, member pack is intentionally read-only for finance:write (403). Expected behavior — tests need updating, product is correct.
PATCH /api/members/{id} now expects {"pack": ...} not {"role": ...}. Old tests send role and get 422. Update tests to send {"pack": "owner"} etc.
Google OAuth is now configured (integrations return configured=true). Tests hard-coded assumption that it was unconfigured. Environment change, not a regression.

issues: Uses native window.confirm() dialog — inconsistent with the rest of the shadcn/dark UI. Consider a themed confirm modal.
Actor name + relative time are on the same row aligned right; on narrow viewports (<400px) the summary text can overlap the timestamp. Minor.

action_items: Update stale iteration-3 tests in test_financials_onboarding.py: member pack should now expect 403 on POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/financials/entries and PUT /api/financials/settings (intended, not a bug).
Update test_kalun_multitenant.py::test_owner_cannot_change_own_role and test_owner_change_member_role_and_delete to send {"pack": ...} instead of {"role": ...} to PATCH /api/members/{id}.
Update test_kalun_multitenant.py OAuth-degradation tests — Google/Quickbooks are now `configured=true` in this env.
(Polish) Replace native window.confirm() on People delete with a themed modal.
(Polish) On Financials 'Recent activity' rows, wrap or truncate long summary text so the actor·time meta doesn't overlap on narrow widths.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_principal still silently reassigns active_workspace_id when the stored active workspace has no matching active membership — repeats iteration_2 note. Consider making this an explicit event so the frontend can react.

server.py add_person/edit_person/remove_person recompute avg_trust by mutating people dict in-place then $set-ing the whole subdoc. If two writers race, one will lose. Not a bug at demo scale but flag it for future.

server.py PATCH /members/{id} accepts arbitrary pack values and silently coerces invalid ones to 'member'. Consider returning 400 on unknown pack so misconfigured clients don't silently downgrade a member.

server.py briefing.what_changed prepends the last 5 activities every time — no de-dup with the workspace's stored what_changed[] items, so on a fresh install the same headline can appear twice (once as activity, once as seeded item). Minor UX.
Frontend Members.jsx: changing a member's pack via <select> has no confirm and no undo. A single misclick can strip a colleague of finance:write. Consider a small confirm toast.
Frontend People.jsx submitted `del(p)` uses window.confirm — see design_issues.

success_rate.backend: 100% for new pack/activity/people suite (20/20); 111/119 overall (8 stale)

test_credentials: OWNER: Bearer test_session_kalun_123 (pack=owner). MEMBER: Bearer test_session_user2 (pack=member, read-only + tasks:move + ask:use). Owner workspace has sample data applied (Northwind Robotics, 6 seed people, 36 fin entries).
seed_data_creation: test_packs_activity_people.py owner fixture idempotently reapplies POST /api/workspace/apply-template {template:sample} at module scope. All test-created data (TEST_ prefixed entries/people, TEST_-prefixed member invites) is cleaned up in-test or via mongo teardown. Frontend UI test added and then deleted its own TEST_UI_ person to restore headcount.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New iteration-4 test file: /app/backend/tests/test_packs_activity_people.py covers Phase 0/1/3 explicitly. Run with `-n 0` (pytest.ini defaults to -n 2 but state-mutating activity/settings tests can interleave). The 8 pre-existing failures in test_financials_onboarding.py + test_kalun_multitenant.py are STALE (member-finance-write assumption + role->pack API shape + Google OAuth now configured). If main agent updates those tests: (a) flip member-finance-write asserts to 403, (b) change PATCH /members payload to {"pack":...}, (c) drop the configured=false assumption. Owner and Member sessions remain seeded (see test_credentials.md).
rca of the issue: No functional issues. Stale-test failures are traceable to intentional product changes shipped in iterations 3→4: (1) member pack lost finance:write, (2) PATCH /members changed role->pack, (3) Google/Quickbooks OAuth got configured in this preview. All three are covered by the new suite.
